column74: The Health Ministry has issued revised guidelines for international arrivals, with effect from February 14, doing away with the mandatory seven-day home quarantine and the need for them to undertake an RT-PCR test on the eighth day.  Apart from uploading a negative RT-PCR report for unvaccinated, taken 72 hours before the journey, there is an option to upload certificates of the completion of the full primary Covid vaccination schedule provided from countries on a reciprocal basis. On arrivals, ALL passengers will undergo thermal screening, and any symptomatic passenger will be isolated as per standard norms. Furthermore, about 2% of overall passengers in any given flight would undergo random testing at the airports on arrival. International travellers arriving through seaports/land ports will also have to undergo the same protocol as above, except that facility for online registration is not available for such passengers currently.    Archived Link: https://web.archive.org/web/20220313200632/https://www.mohfw.gov.in/pdf/GuidelinesforInternationalarrivalsupdatedon10thFebruary2022.pdf

column88: https://web.archive.org/web/20220323132631/https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/MHAOrderCOVIDContainment_25022022.pdf  MHA order dated 25 Feb 2022  "Ensure sustained critical level of testing as per the testing guidelines"    https://archive.ph/jGI1E  ICMR Purposive testing strategy dated 10 Jan 2022  ""People who need not be tested: Contacts of confirmed cases of Covid unless identified as high risk based on age or comorbidities and individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel," read the ICMR Advisory on Purposive Testing Strategy for COVID-19 issued on Monday.  The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

column74: Fully vaccinated individuals will have to produce a final vaccination certificate at the origin airport or seaport at the Port Blair. column74: The Health Ministry has issued revised guidelines for international arrivals, with effect from February 14, doing away with the mandatory seven-day home quarantine and the need for them to undertake an RT-PCR test on the eighth day. Apart from uploading a negative RT-PCR report for unvaccinated, taken 72 hours before the journey, there is an option to upload certificates of the completion of the full primary Covid vaccination schedule provided from countries on a reciprocal basis. On arrivals, ALL passengers will undergo thermal screening, and any symptomatic passenger will be isolated as per standard norms. Furthermore, about 2% of overall passengers in any given flight would undergo random testing at the airports on arrival. International travellers arriving through seaports/land ports will also have to undergo the same protocol as above, except that facility for online registration is not available for such passengers currently. column90: https://archive.ph/jGI1E  ICMR Purposive testing strategy dated 10 Jan 2022  ""People who need not be tested: Contacts of confirmed cases of Covid unless identified as high risk based on age or comorbidities and individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel," read the ICMR Advisory on Purposive Testing Strategy for COVID-19 issued on Monday.  The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

column15: All offices, shops, and business establishments, all religious places, and shopping malls would now be opened in a normal way since february 7 as the Bihar government decided to lift many COVID-19 restrictions citing improvement in pandemic situation. column88: ICMR advisory on purposive testing as of 10 Jan 2022 still stands, allows anyone to procure a RTPCR test   https://archive.vn/F8aFB  "Who may be tested:  A. In community settings:  1. Symptomatic (cough, fever, sore throat, loss of taste and/or smell, breathlessness and/or  other respiratory symptoms) individuals.  2. At-risk contacts of laboratory confirmed cases.  [At-risk contacts are elderly (>60yr) and individuals with co-morbidity such as diabetes,  hypertension, chronic lung or kidney disease, malignancy, obesity etc].  3. Individuals undertaking international travel (as per country-specific requirements).  4. International travelers arriving at Indian airports/seaports/ports of entries as per laid down  guidelines.  B. In Hospital Settings:  5. Testing may be undertaken as per discretion of the treating doctor with the following  considerations:  ? No emergency procedure (including surgeries and deliveries) should be delayed for lack  of a test.  ? Patients should not be referred to other facilities for lack of a testing facility. All  arrangements should be made to collect and transfer samples to testing facilities,  mapped to the health facility.  ? Asymptomatic patients undergoing surgical / non-surgical invasive procedures including  pregnant women in/near labour who are hospitalized for delivery should not be tested  unless warranted or symptoms develop."
column90: https://archive.ph/jGI1E  ICMR Purposive testing strategy dated 10 Jan 2022  ""People who need not be tested: Contacts of confirmed cases of Covid unless identified as high risk based on age or comorbidities and individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel," read the ICMR Advisory on Purposive Testing Strategy for COVID-19 issued on Monday.  The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

column74: The Health Ministry has issued revised guidelines for international arrivals, with effect from February 14, doing away with the mandatory seven-day home quarantine and the need for them to undertake an RT-PCR test on the eighth day.  Apart from uploading a negative RT-PCR report for unvaccinated, taken 72 hours before the journey, there is an option to upload certificates of the completion of the full primary Covid vaccination schedule provided from countries on a reciprocal basis. On arrivals, ALL passengers will undergo thermal screening, and any symptomatic passenger will be isolated as per standard norms. Furthermore, about 2% of overall passengers in any given flight would undergo random testing at the airports on arrival. International travellers arriving through seaports/land ports will also have to undergo the same protocol as above, except that facility for online registration is not available for such passengers currently. column88: https://web.archive.org/web/20220323132631/https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/MHAOrderCOVIDContainment_25022022.pdf  MHA order dated 25 Feb 2022  "Ensure sustained critical level of testing as per the testing guidelines"    https://archive.ph/jGI1E  ICMR Purposive testing strategy dated 10 Jan 2022  ""People who need not be tested: Contacts of confirmed cases of Covid unless identified as high risk based on age or comorbidities and individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel," read the ICMR Advisory on Purposive Testing Strategy for COVID-19 issued on Monday.  The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

column74: India from Monday will no longer require negative RT-PCR test reports from fully vaccinated travellers from 86 countries, according to its revised guidelines on international arrivals. The Health Ministry has issued revised guidelines for international arrivals, with effect from February 14, doing away with the mandatory seven-day home quarantine and the need for them to undertake an RT-PCR test on the eighth day. column74: The Health Ministry has issued revised guidelines for international arrivals, with effect from February 14, doing away with the mandatory seven-day home quarantine and the need for them to undertake an RT-PCR test on the eighth day.  Apart from uploading a negative RT-PCR report for unvaccinated, taken 72 hours before the journey, there is an option to upload certificates of the completion of the full primary Covid vaccination schedule provided from countries on a reciprocal basis. On arrivals, ALL passengers will undergo thermal screening, and any symptomatic passenger will be isolated as per standard norms. Furthermore, about 2% of overall passengers in any given flight would undergo random testing at the airports on arrival. International travellers arriving through seaports/land ports will also have to undergo the same protocol as above, except that facility for online registration is not available for such passengers currently.    Archived Link: https://web.archive.org/web/20220313200632/https://www.mohfw.gov.in/pdf/GuidelinesforInternationalarrivalsupdatedon10thFebruary2022.pdf

column90: https://archive.ph/jGI1E  ICMR Purposive testing strategy dated 10 Jan 2022  ""People who need not be tested: Contacts of confirmed cases of Covid unless identified as high risk based on age or comorbidities and individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel," read the ICMR Advisory on Purposive Testing Strategy for COVID-19 issued on Monday. column90: https://web.archive.org/web/20220323132631/https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/MHAOrderCOVIDContainment_25022022.pdf    https://archive.ph/jGI1E  ICMR Purposive testing strategy dated 10 Jan 2022  ""People who need not be tested: Contacts of confirmed cases of Covid unless identified as high risk based on age or comorbidities and individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel," read the ICMR Advisory on Purposive Testing Strategy for COVID-19 issued on Monday.  The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

All  arrangements should be made to collect and transfer samples to testing facilities,  mapped to the health facility.  ? Apart from uploading a negative RT-PCR report for unvaccinated, taken 72 hours before the journey, there is an option to upload certificates of the completion of the full primary Covid vaccination schedule provided from countries on a reciprocal basis. On arrivals, ALL passengers will undergo thermal screening, and any symptomatic passenger will be isolated as per standard norms. Furthermore, about 2% of overall passengers in any given flight would undergo random testing at the airports on arrival. International travellers arriving through seaports/land ports will also have to undergo the same protocol as above, except that facility for online registration is not available for such passengers currently. column74: As per the Government of India guidelines ( dated 30th November, 2021) , all passengers coming from abroad are required to be quarantined for 7 days.       Travellers from specified Countries at risk [as mentioned in para (iii) above] will follow the protocol as detailed below:  ? Submission of sample for post-arrival COVID-19 test* at the point of arrival (self-paid). Such travellers will be required to wait for their test results at the arrival airport before leaving or taking a connecting flight.  ? If tested negative they will follow, home quarantine for 7 days. Re-test on the 8th day of arrival in India* and if negative, further self-monitor of their health for next 7 days.  ? However, if such travellers are tested positive, their samples should be sent for genomic testing at INSACOG laboratory network.  ? They shall be managed at separate isolation facility and treated as per laid down standard protocol including contact tracing mentioned in para (xiv).  ? The contacts of such positive case should be kept under institutional quarantine or at home quarantine monitored strictly by the concerned State Government as per laid down protocol.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220215055801/https://www.mohfw.gov.in/pdf/GuidelinesforInternationalarrivalsdated30thNovember2021.pdf

column60: There has been total containment orders in Covid-19 hotspots especially in south Sikkim region. The location is subject to change according to the transmission rate in the area. The regions, institutions or housings required to quarantine are mentioned in each circulars. Police task force ensure active patrolling in this areas to prevent any movement of people in containment zones except for medical emergency and supply of essential goods or services.  people in containment zones undergo 11 days of quarantine and if any person fails to comply to these orders are punishable.  The given web archives are from as early as 25/07/2021 to the most recent one on 31/01/2022. There were many others issued each month in several areas of South Sikkim  https://web.archive.org/web/20220203183306/https://cdn.s3waas.gov.in/s38757150decbd89b0f5442ca3db4d0e0e/uploads/2021/07/2021072753.pdf  https://web.archive.org/web/20220204064758/https://cdn.s3waas.gov.in/s38757150decbd89b0f5442ca3db4d0e0e/uploads/2022/02/2022020125.pdf

column15: National overview as of 19 Jan: No nationwide school closure or student vaccine mandate has been imposed by the national govt (“Union govt”/”Centre”). However, several state governments have enacted school closures and other restrictions. While some areas (i.e Tamil Nadu) have enacted vaccine-differentiated restrictions, restrictions in many areas apply regardless of vaccination status.    Coding explanation: Unvaccinated and vaccinated are both coded 3G, to reflect the widespread closures found in at least *29* states/union territories, encompassing several of the most highly-populated regions. Note that vaccine-differentiated policies do exist, but states with such policies (I.e Tamil Nadu) have not yet opened schools for anyone, though it is planned to do so soon (1 Feb, for Tamil Nadu). Therefore, the coding is 3G to reflect how closure for vaccinated and unvaccinated is effectively the same for the time being, due to the same type of restriction (i.e physical closure of schools for everyone regardless of vaccination status). column24: Important note: Addition of vaccine-differentiated coding from this point.     1.	This indicator codes for physical closures/modified workplace requirements. (Example: Total closure of workplace, work-from-home requirements, orders to operate at 50% capacity instead).     2.	Additionally, vaccine-differentiation coding for this indicator records for requirements for visitors/customers to be vaccinated, *not staff/employees.* (Example: “Customers must show proof of vaccination to dine at a restaurant.”)    3.	For vaccine-differentiated measures for *staff/employees of workplaces*, please see indicator *V4* (Vaccine Mandates) instead. (Example: “Mandatory vaccination for restaurant staff.”)     National overview for 19-31 Jan: No nationwide workplace closures or vaccine mandates have been imposed by the national government. column74: For the period of 18—21 January, the protocol for international travellers emphasises differentiation mainly regarding whether the traveller is from an "At Risk" country or not, rather than vaccination status.     1. Screening:   - Regardless of vaccination status, all travellers must have a negative result on their PCR test no more than 72 hours before departure. Travellers must also complete and submit a declaration form on the Air Suvidha Portal.   - Upon arrival, travellers from "Countries Specified At Risk" must take a PCR test and may not leave the airport until they receive their result.  - Travellers who are not from such countries do not ordinarily need to be tested, but PCR tests are carried out on a random sample (2%) of this group.     2. Quarantine: All travellers, regardless of vaccination status and country of origin, must quarantine for 7 days. It is not possible to "test out" of quarantine, even if one tests negative on PCR test taken at the airport.     3. Screening: A final PCR test is required on Day 8, with the result uploaded on the Air Suvidha Portal.    Archived sources:  1. Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Guidelines for International Arrivals; (7th January update, guidelines in effect since 11 January 2022) https://web.archive.org/web/20220112020820/https://www.mohfw.gov.in/pdf/RevisedGuidelinesforInternationalArrivalsdated7thJanuary2022.pdf

column15: Coding change: From 3G to 3T.    Coding explanation: As schools in several (but not all) states have fully or partly reopened on 1 Feb, the school closures have been downgraded from 3G (general) to 3T (targeted). However, please note that vaccine mandates for students do exist in some states that have reopened, but the strictest situation is coded for. The single "3T" coding is due to the *total closure* of schools in some areas as of 1 Feb, that *apply to both the vaccinated and unvaccinated*. Multiple states chose to reopen classes for at least some grades on 1 Feb, albeit with Covid-19 precautions (vaccine mandates for students, masking, sanitisation and social distancing rules). Domestic travelers must hold negative results of a COVID-19 test taken within 48 hours before departure or vaccination certificates. Unvaccinated domestic travelers without pre-departure test results, as well as all entrants with an overseas travel history in the past 30 days, must take an on-arrival PCR test and quarantine until they receive a negative test result. Additional entry, testing, and quarantine rules are likely to enter tribal areas in the Nicobar Islands.    Andhra Pradesh: The 23:00-05:00 nightly curfew is no longer in place. Outdoor and indoor gatherings are capped at 200 and 100 people, respectively. Domestic arrivals must register online up to 72 hours before travel on the Andhra Pradesh police website. Domestic entrants do not require proof of vaccination or pre-departure testing; officials may direct symptomatic arrivals to undergo testing and/or quarantine based on test results.    Karnataka: Demonstrations are banned; permitted gatherings must be limited to 300 people if outdoors, and 200 people if indoors. Most in-person educational classes have resumed. Most venues, including state government offices, as well as dine-in, some recreational, and most sports facilities, may function at full capacity. Only fully vaccinated people can use dine-in, recreational, religious, and sports venues. Checkpoints and interstate transport curbs are most likely in border areas of Belagavi, Chamarajanagar, Dakshina Kannada, Kodagu, and Mysuru districts. Domestic arrivals must register online up to 72 hours before travel. Officials require entrants from Kerala, Goa, and Maharashtra states to provide a vaccine certificate.    Kerala: All arrivals must register online via the Jagratha portal up to 72 hours before travel. Unvaccinated entrants without pre-departure test results must take an on-arrival test and quarantine at home until they test negative or undergo a 14-day home quarantine. Pre-approved domestic travelers leaving the state within seven days are exempt from quarantine. On-arrival testing is limited to symptomatic and randomly selected international travelers. All international entrants are advised to self-monitor their health, submit to symptom surveillance, as well as avoid gatherings and crowded places for seven days from their arrival.    Puducherry: Large public gatherings remain prohibited through March 31, except permitted events such as funerals and weddings. Commercial, educational, and recreational venues, as well as transport services, can operate at full capacity. Retail outlets must ensure employees are vaccinated. Domestic entrants do not require proof of vaccination or pre-departure testing; officials may direct symptomatic arrivals to undergo testing and/or quarantine based on test results.    Tamil Nadu: All in-person educational classes have resumed statewide. Officials have lifted capacity limits on public transport as well as dine-in, grooming, sports, and retail venues. Staff at customer-facing positions and passengers on local suburban trains must be vaccinated. Public gatherings remain banned except for permitted events. Guest limits for weddings and funerals are 200 and 100, respectively. All domestic travelers must register online beforehand; those from Kerala must also carry proof of vaccination or negative pre-departure test results. Interstate travel curbs are possible, mainly to and from Kerala State.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220314103918/https://crisis24.garda.com/alerts/2022/02/india-kerala-state-lifts-most-covid-19-curbs-as-of-march-1-update-47

Anyone who tests positive on arrival will be taken to government isolation facilities, along with anyone seated within three rows of them on the airplane, and relevant cabin crew, whether or not they have tested negative. Before departure, all travelers aged five years and older must upload a self-declaration form on the Air Suvidha Portal. They must also confirm that they will abide by any Covid-19 decisions taken around potential quarantine or testing, and that their declarations are correct. Those who do not qualify, or who do not have the right documentation, must upload a negative PCR test taken within 72 hours of departure.
